patterns.condition: Generating a level, loot or enemies
patterns.action: Create one seed per run, derive the random choices from it, and show or store it, so a bug or a good run can be replayed.

patterns.condition: Placing rooms, doors or spawns at random
patterns.action: After generating, test that start, exit and key items can all be reached, and regenerate or repair when they cannot.
patterns.statement: Always check that a generated level is connected

patterns.condition: Choosing what a chest or enemy drops
patterns.action: Give each entry a weight, roll once against the total, and keep rare items rare, then check a thousand rolls give the spread you want.
patterns.statement: Loot tables use weights, not even odds

patterns.action: Keep a meta currency or an unlock after every run, so a failed run still moves the player forward, and never wipe unlocks on death.
Scale enemy health, damage and count by depth with a gentle curve, and add a harder guardian every few floors.
patterns.statement: Difficulty should rise with depth, not stay flat

patterns.condition: Many systems act in one run
patterns.action: Show health, status effects, the current floor and what an enemy will do next, or players cannot learn from failure.

patterns.condition: Players can quit to avoid dying
patterns.action: Store the run state when the player leaves and mark it as in progress, so quitting never rewinds a death or lets them retry a loss.
Vary rooms, enemies and loot each run while keeping the rules the same, so skill carries over but memory does not solve the map.
patterns.statement: Replay value comes from the world changing

patterns.action: Play ten runs, note which floor ends most runs, and tune that floor until the spread of ending floors looks smooth.
